core_claim: Cortical oscillators in the theta band entrain to amplitude-modulated acoustic input via weak phase coupling.
mechanism: Phase coupling between an external rhythmic drive and an intrinsic theta-band cortical oscillator produces emergent phase locking.
scope: Healthy adults listening to amplitude-modulated tones in the 4-8 Hz range.
main_assumptions: The cortical oscillator is well-approximated by a single-phase oscillator.
Coupling is weak and sinusoidal in the phase difference.
alternatives_ruled_out: Pure transient evoked-response account: predicts no sustained phase locking beyond a few cycles.
distinctive_falsifiable_prediction: Phase-locking value between cortex and stimulus envelope exceeds 0.4 in the 4-8 Hz band over the 100-400 ms post-onset window, robustly across coupling strengths in [1.0, 3.0].
what_would_falsify_it: PLV does not exceed 0.4 anywhere in the [1.0, 3.0] coupling range, OR PLV exceeds 0.4 only at a single coupling value (no robust regime).
